question_text: Write the equation of the plane 4x−4y+2z+5=0 in the intercept form.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what must be on the right-hand side, and what the denominators mean.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Move the constant across
steps.margin_note: First mark. Intercept form needs 1 on the right, so the constant term goes across first and every term is then divided by it.
steps.memory_tip: Intercept form needs 1 on the RIGHT, so move the constant across and divide every term by it.
lines: The given equation of the plane is  4x − 4y + 2z + 5 = 0

recall.must_convey: That the constant is moved to the right and every term divided by it.
accept: move the constant across and divide everything by it
intercept form needs one on the right hand side
divide each term by the number on the right
constant ni right side ki teesi divide cheyyali

steps.why: Intercept form must have 1 on the right-hand side — that is its whole definition. So the constant is moved across and everything divided by it, and the three denominators that appear ARE the intercepts.
common_mistakes: Leaving a number other than 1 on the right.
Dividing only some of the terms.

steps.label: Read off the intercept form
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Once each term reads x over something, that something IS the intercept on that axis. Take care with signs — a negative intercept is perfectly normal.
steps.memory_tip: Once each term reads x over something, that something IS the intercept. A negative intercept is normal.

lines.text: which is in the intercept form x/a + y/b + z/c = 1

recall.must_convey: That dividing by −5 gives x/(−5/4) + y/(5/4) + z/(−5/2) = 1.
accept: read off the three denominators as the intercepts
x over a plus y over b plus z over c equals one

steps.why: The intercept on an axis is where the plane cuts it, which is found by setting the other two coordinates to zero — and the intercept form displays all three at once.
common_mistakes: Reading the numerator as the intercept.
Losing a minus sign on a negative intercept.

insider_note: Move the 5 across first, then divide by −5 so the right side is exactly 1. The intercept is the denominator that results, so a = −5/4, and the middle term's two minus signs leave b positive.
